title: F0 Knockout Protocol for Single Gene Disruption
author: Francois Kroll
materials: Annealing In small PCR tubes; 1 µL crRNA 200 micromolar (µM) 1 µL tracrRNA 200 micromolar (µM) 1.28 µL Duplex buffer Total 3.28 µL One for each crRNA; typically 3x. Place in a thermocycler: 95 °C for 00:05:00 crRNA annealed to tracrRNA is gRNA; now at 61 micromolar (µM)

steps.title: Select crRNAs for gene knockout
steps.instruction: Choose three crRNAs that target the gene at distinct sites (preferably on the same exon if the gene has one or two exons) and avoid overlap of binding sites or PAM sequences. Follow the external protocol “How to select the best gRNA(s) for frameshift knockouts in zebrafish” (dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.81wgb6r5qlpk/v1) for detailed design criteria.

steps.title: Resuspend crRNA and tracrRNA on ice
steps.instruction: Keep all tubes on ice, spin down the lyophilized crRNA and tracrRNA vials so pellets are at the bottom. Resuspend 2 nmol crRNA in 10 µL Duplex Buffer (200 µM stock) and 5 nmol tracrRNA in 25 µL Duplex Buffer (200 µM stock). Vortex briefly and spin down a couple of times. Aliquot the resuspended crRNA into ~4 µL portions and the tracrRNA into ~10 µL portions, each aliquot to be used a maximum of three times; mark the Eppendorf tubes to track usage. Store all aliquots at –80 °C. Reagents: crRNA (IDT custom order), tracrRNA (IDT catalog #1072532), Duplex Buffer (IDT catalog #11-01-03-01, shipped with tracrRNA).

substeps.instruction: Spin down vials on ice to collect pellets.
Resuspend 2 nmol crRNA in 10 µL Duplex Buffer (200 µM).
Resuspend 5 nmol tracrRNA in 25 µL Duplex Buffer (200 µM).
Vortex and spin down a few times.
Aliquot crRNA (~4 µL) and tracrRNA (~10 µL) into labeled tubes.
Store aliquots at –80 °C.

steps.title: Assemble RNP complexes
steps.instruction: In each PCR tube add 1 µL of a specific gRNA (crRNA + tracrRNA) and 1 µL Cas9 protein (61 µM) for a total volume of 2 µL per RNP. Prepare one tube per crRNA (typically three tubes). Place the tubes in a thermocycler at 37 °C for 5 minutes to allow RNP formation. The resulting RNP concentration is 30.5 µM.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 µL gRNA to a PCR tube.
Add 1 µL Cas9 (61 µM) to the same tube.
Mix gently and incubate at 37 °C for 5 minutes.
Resulting RNP concentration = 30.5 µM.

steps.title: Pool and aliquot RNPs
steps.instruction: Pool 2 µL (or the entire volume) from each assembled RNP tube; with three crRNAs this yields ~6 µL total pooled RNP at 30.5 µM (each individual RNP at 10.1 µM). The pooled RNP can be stored at 4 °C, –20 °C, or –80 °C for at least 10 weeks without loss of activity. Recommended practice: prepare the pool the evening before injection, split the 6 µL into two ~3 µL aliquots, keep one at 4 °C for next‑day injection and the other at –80 °C for future use. Discard any aliquot after it has been used to avoid freeze‑thaw damage. If desired, split into three 2 µL aliquots, but note that 2 µL may be too low for needle re‑loading.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 2 µL (or all) from each RNP tube into a single tube.
Mix to obtain ~6 µL pooled RNP (30.5 µM total, 10.1 µM per RNP).
Aliquot pooled RNP into two ~3 µL portions.
Store one aliquot at 4 °C for next‑day injection; store the other at –80 °C for long‑term use.
Avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles; discard used aliquot after injection.

steps.title: Inject embryos with RNP mix
steps.instruction: Inject 1 nL of the RNP solution into the yolk of each zebrafish embryo at the single‑cell stage before the cell inflates (cell should be flat and wrapped around the yolk). If the cell has already inflated or divided, discard that clutch and start with fresh eggs. The injection mix contains 30.5 fmol (5 029 pg) Cas9 and 30.5 fmol (1 070 pg) gRNA for a 3× setup; each individual gRNA contributes 10.1 fmol (357 pg). The solution creates a brief black stain in the yolk, which serves as a successful‑injection marker; no phenol‑red dye is needed. Prepare injection set‑up (calibrate needles) and, after removing the divider from breeding boxes, wait 7–8 minutes before collecting eggs. Inject all eggs within the first 20 minutes after they are laid; if any begin inflating or dividing, begin a new clutch.

substeps.instruction: Calibrate injection needles and set up injection apparatus.
Remove divider from breeding boxes, wait 7–8 minutes, then collect freshly laid eggs.
Inject 1 nL of pooled RNP (30.5 fmol Cas9, 30.5 fmol gRNA) into the centre of the yolk of each single‑cell embryo.
Observe the transient black stain in the yolk as confirmation of successful injection; do not add phenol‑red dye.
Complete injections within ~20 minutes after egg laying; discard any embryos that have already inflated or divided and start with a new clutch.
